html:
A domed church in Constantinople built by Justinian and Theodora and dedicated to the Syrian soldier saints Sergius and Bacchus. Its date is disputed: some scholars say it was started by 527, others place it between 532 and 536.

It stood next to the palace where Justinian lived before he became emperor. The plan is an octagon under a dome, set inside a square, with a gallery above. A carved inscription running round the inside honours Justinian and his "God crowned" empress. Its layout is close to that of San Vitale in Ravenna, and it is often seen as a trial run for the much bigger Hagia Sophia, hence the nickname.

Around 1500, under the Ottomans, it was turned into a mosque, which it still is.
